name: Birdeye
description: The dominant Solana market data API providing OHLCV, token prices, wallet portfolio P&L, and trader analytics. Primary market context layer for Solana trading agents and DeFi dashboards.

ecosystem_fit.notes: The default market data provider for Solana trading agents. Birdeye aggregates DEX trade data from Jupiter, Raydium, Orca and exposes it as structured market analytics.
Birdeye has Base/EVM coverage but is not the dominant choice there. CoinGecko and DefiLlama serve EVM market data more broadly.
EVM coverage exists but the product is Solana-native. Use CoinGecko or DefiLlama for Ethereum-first market data needs.

common_pairings.context: Helius provides raw onchain event data (transactions, account state); Birdeye provides the derived market interpretation (what was the price during that transaction, what is the wallet's P&L). In a trading agent, both are required — Helius for triggers, Birdeye for context.
Birdeye data feeds into the agent's market context window. The agent framework consumes Birdeye price/P&L data to reason about trade decisions.

Birdeye provides price context and route evaluation; Jupiter executes the actual swap. A trading agent uses Birdeye to decide whether to trade and at what price threshold, then Jupiter to compute the optimal route.
Birdeye API calls are made within Trigger.dev job steps. Price context fetching is an observable, retriable step in the agent execution pipeline.

trust_evidence.description: Birdeye is the most cited Solana market data API in trading agent repositories. Appears consistently in Solana AI agent stacks alongside Helius and Jupiter.
Listed as the primary market-data tool in the canonical solana-trading-agent workflow. No competing tool at equivalent coverage for Solana market analytics.
Birdeye provides a public REST API with documented endpoints for price, OHLCV, wallet P&L, and token analytics. API key required for production use.
Integrated by multiple Solana trading agent frameworks including sendaifun's Eliza plugins. Referenced in Solana trading agent tutorials and production repositories.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Use Birdeye's public API with a free-tier API key. Rate limits are acceptable for demo workloads.
scale_guidance.mvp: Implement response caching for price queries — Birdeye rate limits are strict and price data has acceptable staleness for most trading decisions (1-5 second cache).
scale_guidance.production: Model API cost against query volume. High-frequency trading agents that call Birdeye on every chain event will exhaust free tiers quickly. Cache aggressively. Consider paying for a higher API tier before scaling.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: When raw onchain state (transaction history, account data) is needed rather than derived market analytics. Helius reads chain state; Birdeye reads market conditions derived from that state. Use both together in trading agents — they are complementary, not alternatives.

anti_patterns: Using Birdeye as the primary Solana chain-data source — Birdeye provides market analytics, not raw onchain state. Transaction history, account balances, and NFT data require Helius or another Solana RPC.
Calling Birdeye on every Helius webhook without caching — price data has acceptable staleness for most agent decisions. Uncached per-event Birdeye calls exhaust rate limits at production volume.
Treating Birdeye prices as authoritative for trade execution — Birdeye aggregates prices from DEX data with potential lag. Use Jupiter's quote API for the actual execution price at time of trade.
Using Birdeye for EVM chains as a primary data source — CoinGecko and DefiLlama have broader and more reliable EVM market data.
